sources.detail: The frozen current Atom query can be captured prospectively before the horizon. This does not convert later submittedDate filtering into historical index-state proof. Any future source-native OAI/incremental mechanism is supplemental unless separately shown to preserve the frozen arm semantics.

A prospectively completed and externally timestamped snapshot avoids relying on Git commit author/committer timestamps as public-availability proof. Same-authority mirror history alone remains insufficient.

The frozen DOC query can be captured prospectively. STARTDATETIME/ENDDATETIME publication bounds are not substituted for collection-state proof because GDELT documents that scoring changes may be applied retroactively to its backfile.

The frozen mutable repository-search result can be captured prospectively before the horizon. Current repository metadata or date qualifiers remain insufficient to reconstruct historical result membership and ordering later.

The frozen current model-list query can be captured prospectively. Hub list/search and repo webhooks provide current or incremental information but do not establish an arbitrary historical global-model ranking for later reconstruction.

The frozen current front-page RSS collection can be captured prospectively before the horizon. The official Firebase API exposes live ranking/change state but no reviewed arbitrary historical front-page membership/ranking query.

The frozen Latest Updates RSS can be captured prospectively. PyPI's Index API exposes monotonic X-PyPI-Last-Serial metadata that can strengthen snapshot diagnostics, but it does not silently replace the frozen RSS arm definition.
